framework: NIST AI Risk Management Framework 1.0 (NIST AI 100-1), with the Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
scope: How Papyrus, as the agent runtime an organization deploys, supports the organization's AI risk management. Most AI RMF outcomes are organizational; Papyrus supplies the mechanisms and records that make them practicable and evidences them. Responsibility follows the same shared model as the 800-53 matrix.

subcategories.title: Risk management process established through transparent policies and controls
subcategories.statement: Every named agent is a versioned configuration (instructions, model, limits, channels) signed by its creator with a one-time key certified by the deployment after a fresh sign-in. With Require agent sign-off on, a different person holding Agents.Approve must also sign before it can be activated. Only an active, signed revision runs.
subcategories.customer: Decide when independent sign-off is required and who may approve agents.

subcategories.title: Inventory of AI systems
subcategories.statement: The Agent Roster lists every agent with its state (draft, awaiting approval, active, paused, archived), revision history, model, signatures and sessions. Requests groups each agent's revisions with their approval status.
subcategories.customer: Review the roster as part of the organization's AI inventory.

evidence.note: Revisions grouped by agent with status

subcategories.title: Decommissioning AI systems safely
subcategories.statement: An agent can be paused or archived. Archiving deactivates it, so its sessions start no new runs, while its revisions, approvals and evidence are kept; a restored agent must be activated again.
subcategories.customer: Archive agents that are no longer approved for use.

verification.note: Archive deactivates and restore requires activation

subcategories.title: Roles, responsibilities and lines of communication documented
subcategories.statement: Authority is split into declared Papyrus roles (including Agents.Create, Agents.Approve, Agents.Activate, Action.Approve and Audit.View), mapped from identity-provider groups in papyrus.yaml. An agent's creator and its independent approver are recorded by identity on every revision.
subcategories.customer: Assign roles in the identity provider to match the organization's AI governance structure.

subcategories.title: Policies define human-AI configurations and oversight
subcategories.statement: Agents propose consequential actions; people approve them. Action approvals require a human with Action.Approve, workflow approval gates are answered only by the person or group they name, tool permissions decide which calls ask first, and agents can ask the person a question and wait.
subcategories.customer: Set which tools and MCP servers require approval, and use approval gates in workflows that act outside Papyrus.

subcategories.title: Practices for testing, incident identification and information sharing
subcategories.statement: Security events and agent activity are recorded in an append-only audit trail and agent traces, exportable to the organization's SIEM over OTLP.
subcategories.customer: Include AI incidents in the organization's incident response plan and route audit records to its SIEM.
subcategories.gap: Beag Labs has no published process for notifying customers of product security incidents.

subcategories.title: Policies address risks from third-party AI (models, data, software)
subcategories.statement: Models are reached only through gateways the organization lists in papyrus.yaml; the government and disconnected profiles never fall back to a commercial model endpoint. Third-party software is inventoried in SPDX and CycloneDX SBOMs, and the release image is signed with build provenance.
subcategories.customer: Choose and approve model providers and models; review the SBOMs.

subcategories.title: Intended purposes, context and settings documented
subcategories.statement: Each agent revision records its name, description, instructions, model, execution profile and goal, and the signature covers exactly that configuration.
subcategories.customer: Write each agent's purpose and constraints into its description and instructions before signing.

subcategories.title: Processes for human oversight defined
subcategories.statement: Oversight is built into the run: approval gates pause workflows until a named person decides, action proposals wait for an approver, and the Inbox and notify_user bring the decision to the person.
subcategories.customer: Define who oversees each agent and workflow.

subcategories.title: Approaches for mapping legal risks of AI components and third-party data
subcategories.statement: Papyrus keeps all prompts, documents and outputs inside the deploying organization's boundary and sends nothing to Beag Labs. The legal review of models and data the organization connects is the organization's.
subcategories.customer: Review model licenses, data rights and connected systems.

evidence.note: No deployment data to Beag Labs

subcategories.title: Functionality and behavior monitored in production
subcategories.statement: Every agent run records its steps, tool calls, outcome and compute, and traces are kept in an observability store. Security-relevant events go to the audit trail.
subcategories.customer: Review runs, traces and audit records on the organization's cadence.

subcategories.title: Security and resilience evaluated and documented
subcategories.statement: Agent code runs in a kernel sandbox with no network; outbound requests pass an egress allow-list; the image runs in FIPS mode and is STIG-scanned. The NIST SP 800-53 matrix in this pack documents each control with source evidence.
subcategories.customer: Include Papyrus in the system's security assessment.
subcategories.gap: No independent penetration test or adversarial (red-team) evaluation of agent behavior has been performed.

subcategories.title: Transparency and accountability risks examined
subcategories.statement: Every agent action is attributed to the person it ran for; revisions carry verifiable signatures and the revision a session runs is shown in its header; the audit trail records who did what, from where.
subcategories.customer: Retain signatures and audit records for the organization's retention period.

evidence.note: Actor and on-behalf-of in each record
MCP calls attributed to the person

subcategories.title: Privacy risk examined
subcategories.statement: Papyrus runs inside the organization's environment and calls no Beag Labs service; credentials are never shown to models; secrets in configuration are references, never values.
subcategories.customer: Assess privacy for the data the organization processes with agents.

subcategories.title: Fairness and bias evaluated
subcategories.statement: Papyrus does not train or fine-tune models and does not evaluate model bias. Offline evaluations in Beag Labs CI check agent task behavior, not fairness.
subcategories.customer: Evaluate the chosen models for the organization's use cases.

subcategories.title: Mechanisms to sustain the value of deployed AI
subcategories.statement: Each agent runs within signed limits: steps, tool calls, wall-clock time, compute time, storage and run count, enforced on every step and tool call; long-running work is handed to background tasks with their own deadlines.
subcategories.customer: Set limits proportionate to each agent's purpose.

evidence.note: Budget enforcement in beforeStep and beforeTool

subcategories.title: Mechanisms to supersede, disengage or deactivate AI systems
subcategories.statement: An agent can be paused at once, archived, or replaced by a new signed revision; API keys can be revoked; portal sessions end on sign-out and after inactivity.
subcategories.customer: Use these controls in response procedures.

subcategories.title: Third-party AI risks monitored and controls applied
subcategories.statement: Model gateways are tested before use and their configuration is recorded at each start; MCP servers are verified and their tools classified by an administrator, which decides whether calls need approval.
subcategories.customer: Review gateway and MCP configuration changes.

subcategories.title: Post-deployment monitoring plans implemented
subcategories.statement: Audit records stream to the organization's collector over OTLP with at-least-once delivery, and the Audit page shows export health and a backlog after outages.
subcategories.customer: Monitor the collector and act on alerts.

generativeAi.response: Tool results from MCP servers and documents are labeled as untrusted external content; agent code has no network; outbound requests pass the egress allow-list; consequential actions need human approval.
Agents cite Library passages with source path, page and SHA-256; consequential outputs go through approval; goal completion is declared with a recorded summary of evidence.
Prompts, documents and outputs stay inside the deploying organization's environment; Beag Labs receives no deployment data.
Models are chosen by the organization in papyrus.yaml; dependencies are inventoried in SBOMs; the release image is signed with build provenance.
Signed agent revisions, optional independent sign-off, approval gates and per-agent limits keep a person accountable for what each agent may do.
